have this code for this question:
Let B_n denote the triangular book graph on n+2 vertices, i.e. with n triangular "pages".

Find an algorithm that takes n as input and produces a graph on 4n - 2 vertices that does not contain a copy of B_{n-1} and whose complement does not contain a copy of B_{n}.

Provide the algorithm that takes n as input and outputs the graph as an adjacency string: a binary string that lists whether an edge is present (1) or absent (0) in column major order, zero-indexed. The order the edges should appear in the string is: {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,3}, {1,3}, {2,3}, {0,4}, {1,4}, {2,4}, {3,4}, ... For example, the string 011010 would represent the 4-vertex graph with edges {0,2}, {1,2}, {1,3}.

Solution format:
* Write a Python script defining a function .
* Do not include any code at the file level. You may include a  block for testing, but it will not be executed by the verifier.
* For n ≤ 100, the algorithm must complete within 10 minutes when run on a typical laptop.

framings.reframing: View the witness family as a Cayley or circulant graph problem: choose a symmetric generator set on a group of size 4n - 2 so that every difference class has tightly controlled codegree.
framings.key_insight: A triangular book is determined by common-neighbor counts, and in a Cayley graph those counts are algebraic correlation values of the generator set.
framings.suggested_technique: Deterministic Cayley or circulant constructions, optionally seeded by conference-matrix or Seidel-switching templates.
framings.mapping_back: Represent vertices by group elements, connect x to y when y - x lies in a symmetric set S, and choose S so every allowed difference has bounded correlation; the resulting rule emits adjacency bits in pure Python without randomized search.

framings.reframing: Treat the graph as a periodic binary waveform wrapped around a circle, where a book violation is a large sidelobe in the correlation profile between shifts.
framings.key_insight: For circulant graphs, the number of common neighbors of a pair depends only on the periodic autocorrelation of the binary support sequence at the corresponding shift.
framings.suggested_technique: Low-autocorrelation binary sequences, cyclic difference sets, or Legendre-type sequence constructions from signal design.
framings.mapping_back: Build a symmetric binary sequence of length 4n - 2, use cyclic shifts to define adjacency, and exact-check whether every shift correlation stays below the B_{n-1} and B_n thresholds.

framings.reframing: Neighborhoods become blocks in a partially balanced experiment, and forbidden books mean no pair of treatments may co-occur in too many blocks.
framings.key_insight: The problem naturally splits pairs into two classes, edge and nonedge, which matches the language of PBIB and quasi-symmetric designs with controlled intersection numbers.
framings.suggested_technique: Partially balanced incomplete block designs or quasi-symmetric 2-designs with two intersection numbers.
framings.mapping_back: Treat each vertex neighborhood as a block family, tune pairwise block intersections to mirror adjacent and nonadjacent codegree ceilings, then reconstruct a symmetric adjacency relation from the resulting incidence structure.

framings.reframing: Each row of the adjacency matrix is a binary codeword, and avoiding books means keeping pairwise overlaps of codewords under tight control.
framings.key_insight: Two-weight codes and bounded-intersection code families already package the same requirement of many binary vectors with limited mutual overlap.
framings.suggested_technique: Two-weight linear codes, constant-weight codes, and association-scheme bounds on pairwise intersections.
framings.mapping_back: Use a code family whose distance distribution takes only a few values, derive a graph from codewords or cosets, and translate overlap bounds into exact common-neighbor bounds before serializing the graph as the adjacency string.

framings.reframing: Encode the graph by a plus-minus-one Seidel matrix and read its rows as vectors on a sphere; the search becomes one for a two-distance point set with controlled inner products.
framings.key_insight: Common-neighbor counts are affine transforms of row inner products, so spherical-code constraints speak directly to book suppression.
framings.suggested_technique: Spherical two-distance codes, equiangular-line constructions, or Gram-matrix search guided by Welch-type bounds.
framings.mapping_back: Search for a symmetric plus-minus-one matrix with acceptable off-diagonal inner products, decode the sign pattern back into edges, and emit the upper-triangular adjacency bits deterministically in Python.

framings.reframing: The rejected probabilistic solver is really a discrepancy-balancing argument waiting to be made constructive.
framings.key_insight: Random half-dense graphs work because pairwise correlations concentrate near expectation; discrepancy methods turn that concentration into deterministic edge decisions.
framings.suggested_technique: Method of conditional probabilities with pessimistic estimators, optionally supported by limited-independence generators.
framings.mapping_back: Expose edge variables one by one, always choosing the bit that keeps the estimated worst codegree violation smallest in G and its complement, so the final output is deterministic rather than Monte Carlo.

framings.reframing: Model the task as an exact Boolean feasibility problem over the upper triangle of the adjacency matrix.
framings.key_insight: A book centered on a pair {u,v} is just a cardinality constraint on shared neighbors, so the full specification is SAT and CP native.
framings.suggested_technique: CP-SAT or SAT encoding with lex-leader symmetry breaking or SAT-modulo-symmetries.
framings.mapping_back: Create one Boolean variable per edge, add constraints bounding common neighbors for each pair in G and its complement, break vertex-permutation symmetry, and serialize any satisfying assignment as the requested string.

framings.reframing: Seek a density one-half pseudorandom graph with no large codegree spikes on either edges or nonedges.
framings.key_insight: Book size is exactly an edge-side or nonedge-side codegree spike, so quasirandomness criteria turn the ban into spectral or jumbledness targets.
framings.suggested_technique: Expander-mixing or jumbledness analysis together with Chung-Graham-Wilson style quasirandom criteria.
framings.mapping_back: Search deterministic regular or near-regular graph families whose second eigenvalue or codegree discrepancy forces all common-neighbor counts into the safe range, then emit that family by formula in pure Python.

framings.reframing: The real deliverable is not a lucky witness but a certified pure-Python function with an explicit correctness contract.
framings.key_insight: Because the failure mode was mixed-language heuristics, the right abstraction is synthesis plus proof obligation rather than one-off search.
framings.suggested_technique: Counterexample-guided inductive synthesis, solver-aided programming, or proof-carrying witness generation.
framings.mapping_back: Sketch a Python constructor family, use forbidden-book counterexamples to refine it, and ship the final function together with an exact verifier over every emitted instance.

framings.reframing: Books are edge-centered triangle motifs, so the task becomes motif engineering under a simultaneous complement-side cap.
framings.key_insight: Local edge switches can sharply reduce the worst spine-triangle multiplicity without discarding a globally regular seed structure.
framings.suggested_technique: Triangle-switch or motif-aware edge-swap neighborhoods with exact acceptance rules.
framings.mapping_back: Start from a deterministic regular or circulant seed, apply only deterministic switches that strictly reduce the maximum book count in G or its complement, and stop only when the exact checker passes.

framings.reframing: Choose adjacency from a Boolean function engineered for flat correlation rather than from ad hoc search.
framings.key_insight: Bent and plateaued Boolean functions are designed to suppress derivative and correlation spikes, and their Cayley graphs inherit very regular common-neighbor structure.
framings.suggested_technique: Bent or plateaued Boolean functions followed by Cayley-graph construction on F_2^m or related groups.
framings.mapping_back: Generate edges by evaluating a Boolean function on vertex differences or labels, exploit bitwise Python implementation for speed, and use exact checks or small deterministic gadgets to adapt the family to order 4n - 2.
